primary_question: Do taxa occupying more different present-day BIO1/BIO4/BIO12/BIO15 climates also differ more in exact-concept corolla LAB lightness?

secondary_directional_screen.interpretation: BIO15 has a consistent negative descriptive direction but does not pass the exact two-sided 0.05 screen in either subset.

decision.reason: The preregistered-in-branch primary association is negative rather than positive in both evidence-depth subsets; exact positive-tail p-values are 0.822 and 0.692, and every n>=5 leave-one-out primary association is negative.
decision.scientific_interpretation: The simplest explanation that phylogenetically distant taxa reoccupy similar lightness because they track similarity in current BIO1/BIO4/BIO12/BIO15 climate is not supported by the present six-/five-taxon data. The lightness overdispersion remains unexplained by these four current-climate axes.

next_inference_boundary: Do not turn this null gate into evidence against climate adaptation generally. Candidate explanations still include unmeasured abiotic axes, historical rather than current climate, biotic interactions, population-level colour variation and other forms of modular trait evolution.
claim_boundary: Exploratory species-level follow-up only. Colour and environment are separate evidence layers and not paired individuals; the tree is in substitutions/site, not time. No adaptation, convergence, causal-climate, ancestral-colour or evolutionary-rate claim is made.
